answer: A meadow holds only so many nests, so admission must be rationed. Each identity needs two holders outside its own patch to countersign its nest, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one cooperative crew. Every nest is priced by rank: the k-th nest an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A forge stamps each nest with a velvet seal recording its signers, and an audit re-asks a random witness; an unconfirmed nest voids the patch and forfeits every bond on it.
